items.exemplar:
A. Nixon's 'law and order' campaign (1968) and 'Southern strategy' courted voters alienated by civil rights, urban riots, and antiwar protest.

B. Reagan's election (1980) sealed the turn: tax cuts, deregulation, and attacks on 'big government' embodied a new conservative governing creed.

C. Cold War approaches varied: Nixon and Kissinger pursued détente with Moscow and the opening to China, while Reagan confronted the 'evil empire' with an arms buildup.
parts: A. Briefly explain ONE example of the conservative direction of the nation in the 1970s and 1980s.
B. Briefly explain a SECOND example of that conservative direction.
C. Briefly explain ONE Cold War approach taken by a 1970s or 1980s president.
items.stimulus: Historian Lisa McGirr argues that the late twentieth century saw 'the triumph of a new conservatism' — as suburban activists, evangelical Christians, and free-market economists reshaped American politics from the grassroots up.
